# Events and timing {#sec-events}

biyos never writes to standard output or standard error. Everything it has to say, a message, a failed check or the time a phase took, is an event on the environment's stream. A program receives events by attaching a function to them, a hook. An event no hook wants is not built.

## Kinds and levels {#sec-events-kinds}

Every event has a kind:

| Kind | Carries |
| --- | --- |
| `BIYOS_EVTKND_MSG` | a message |
| `BIYOS_EVTKND_INV` | a failed check |
| `BIYOS_EVTKND_SPAN` | a phase beginning or ending, with its time |

It also has a level, from `BIYOS_EVTLVL_DBG` up to `BIYOS_EVTLVL_ERR`, the module that sent it, such as `capi`, a text and a list of named fields.

## Hooks {#sec-events-hooks}

`BIYOS_addenvhook` attaches a hook to one kind of event at a lowest level. The hook then receives every event of that kind at that level or above:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/events.c" item="hook"}
```

The call gives an id, and `BIYOS_delenvhook` removes the hook by it. Hooks receive an event in the order they were added, one at a time even when events come from several threads ([Threads](#sec-threads)).

`BIYOS_addmdlhook` attaches a hook to one model instead. It receives the events of calls on that model, before the hooks of the environment do:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/events.c" item="hook_model"}
```

A model's hooks are freed with it, and a copy does not inherit them ([Copying models](#sec-copy)). The example adds two hooks to the environment and one to a model, then makes a call on the model fail:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/events.c" item="main"}
```

## Formatting an event {#sec-events-format}

`BIYOS_fmttext` writes an event as one line for people, and `BIYOS_fmtjson` as one JSON object for tools. Both work like `snprintf`, with the size before the buffer. A size of 0 only reports the length, so a hook can size its buffer exactly:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/events.c" item="print_json"}
```

The failed call of the example gives these lines:

```text
0.000125 error capi: invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647] code=-100
{"time":0.000125,"kind":"message","level":"error","module":"capi","text":"invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647]","fields":{"code":"-100"}}
```

The time is in seconds since the environment was created.

## Reading an event {#sec-events-read}

A hook can also read an event part by part, with `BIYOS_getevtknd`, `BIYOS_getevtlvl`, `BIYOS_getevttext` and the other readers of [Events](#sec-capi-events). This function finds the status code an error message carries:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/events.c" item="code_of"}
```

## The events biyos sends {#sec-events-sent}

Every failed call sends an error message from `capi`, with the status in its field `code`, so one hook sees every failure. Other messages come from deprecated options ([Versions](#sec-options-versions)), from oddities met while reading or writing a file ([File formats](#sec-formats)) and from `BIYOS_cmpmdl` when two models differ.

A failed check is sent when `checking` finds an invariant that does not hold, and the call then fails. Today the one check is that a callback leaves its outputs finite. A span marks a phase, such as reading a file, beginning or ending, with its wall and CPU time. [Error codes and events](#sec-codes) describes every event field by field.

## Inside a hook {#sec-events-inside}

While a hook runs, the environment and its models are read-only to the hook's thread. The hook may read options, the last error, the event and the models, and a call that would change any of them fails with `BIYOS_ERR_BADARG`. The event and the strings read from it are valid only until the hook returns.

## Events in Python {#sec-events-python}

`env.addhook` attaches any callable that takes one `Event`, and `model.addhook` does the same for one model. The event's properties, such as `kind`, `level` and `text`, read its parts, and `fmttext` and `fmtjson` give its lines. Forwarding events to Python's `logging` takes a few lines:

```{.python file="examples/code/python/events.py"}
```

An exception raised in a hook does not escape into C. biyos raises it in the program once the call that sent the event returns.
